Also: freeze panes corrected from A50 (which froze the first 49 rows) to A2, and two stale merged ranges removed — A43:F43 and A57:F57 survived the row deletion and silently masked columns B-F on those rows, dropping the Column_Name for Indicator Framework.Official_Link and SDG Goal Lookup.Used_In_Workbook until they were rewritten. v15: Indicator Framework — Policy_Goal_Summary renamed Policy_Purpose and revalued from each framework's own primary documentation. The former values were semicolon-delimited lists of policy instruments rather than summaries, and several had absorbed indicator-level detail through aggregation of the Policy_Goal field: IFW-02 ended "Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity (GBF-T8)" and IFW-07 read "GBF Goal A and Targets 2, 8, 11; SDG 15.5", neither of which described the framework. IFW-04 implied State of Nature reports against the GBF, which it does not — it is an independent NGO-led assessment with no statutory targets. New values are 565-808 characters of prose covering purpose and policy range, sourced and reviewed in outputs_other/policy_goal_summary_review/. New column Key_Instruments holds bracketed governance codes ONLY (no names) for the instruments and organisations named in Policy_Purpose — normally the body creating, hosting or using the framework, its statutory basis where it has one, and the key policies or international instruments it informs. All 34 codes were validated against the governance registry before writing. It was APPENDED, not inserted (see the v12 note on insert_cols and hyperlinks). Column widths and row heights for the sheet were refitted to the longer text, cap raised to 300pt for this sheet only. Data Dictionary updated IN PLACE per the v14 convention. NOT CHANGED, by decision: Source_Framework for IFW-09 still reads "EEA Biodiversity Strategy Indicators" although the EEA publishes no set under that title. MEDIUM CONFIDENCE: the IFW-01 clause stating that the OEP scrutinises the EIP progress report is well established but was not found on the EIF pages themselves.

v17: Framework currency check against published sources (EIF theme pages A-K on gov.uk; CCC Mitigation and Adaptation Monitoring Framework pages). (1) EIF verified CURRENT: all 66 held codes and names match the published set one for one, no additions or retirements; the six 2026 updates were data refreshes, Defra having moved the EIF off an annual cycle to rolling updates. IFW-01 Official_Link repointed from oifdata.defra.gov.uk (now a redirect) to the gov.uk collection. Two names corrected to the published wording: IND-E-037 gains "the" before "annual growth"; IND-E-052 gains "against a baseline". (2) IFW-02 SPLIT. The CCC now publishes mitigation and adaptation as separate frameworks on separate cycles, and the row-level Source_Framework values already distinguished them (79 mitigation / 32 adaptation), so only the register row conflated them. IFW-02 is now mitigation only (79 records, published June 2025 updated June 2026); new IFW-10 holds adaptation (32 records). Both point at Sheet_Name "CCC Indicators" - nothing keys on Sheet_Name as a unique value: the governance diagram keys on Framework_ID and the indicator finder carries its own hardcoded FRAMEWORKS/FRAMEWORK_CTX tables, so both halves continue to resolve the same governance chain. (3) The CCC mitigation benchmark moved from the Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023 to the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (October 2025). 24 rows citing the CBDP are annotated in Source_Reference; their benchmark figures were NOT re-derived, because doing so requires reading the CBGDP and would be a value judgement rather than a mechanical edit. (4) The 32 adaptation rows are flagged as the 2023-2025 set: the May 2026 rebuild is anchored on CCRA4-IA, takes its ambition from the 21 objectives in A Well-Adapted UK, and restructures monitoring around fourteen systems, nine of which have no held rows. Re-extraction is queued, not attempted here.

v18: Nine CCC mitigation benchmarks re-derived against the Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan (October 2025) and the CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report, clearing the SUPERSEDED marker from 9 of the 24 rows annotated in v17. Buildings and surface transport were done first because the CCC states the CBGDP reduces emissions more slowly than the CBDP 2023 in exactly these two sectors. SUBSTANTIVE CHANGES, not restatements: IND-C-021 heat pumps - the Heat and Buildings Strategy target of 600,000/year by 2028 is gone, replaced by the Warm Homes Plan goal of 450,000/year UK-wide by 2030 of which ~250,000 retrofit, which the CCC says is itself insufficient for the CBGDP; the CCC Balanced Pathway figure is restated as ~1.4 million retrofit/year by 2035. IND-C-022 EPC - "all homes EPC C by 2035" is no longer government policy; the benchmark is now the planned Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (private rented to EPC C on two metrics by 2030, social rented one metric by 2030 and two by 2039), with the affected housing numbers. IND-C-023 insulation - the ECO4 scheme named in the old benchmark has closed with no replacement; there is no quantified government insulation target, and the CCC now tracks cavity wall insulation coverage. IND-C-027 non-residential - records the closure of the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme and the still-unconfirmed EPC B by 2030 non-residential MEES. IND-C-018 chargepoints - the 300,000 by 2030 target is UNCHANGED and confirmed on track, with the 2025 figure added. IND-C-016 electric vans - rebenchmarked on CBGDP uptake assumptions, with the 2025 actual (9.5% of new van sales). IND-C-003, IND-C-019 and IND-C-025 - sectoral pathway rows repointed from the CBDP to the CBGDP. FIFTEEN ROWS STILL CARRY THE MARKER: electricity supply, industry, agriculture and land use, aviation, waste and cross-economy. Those benchmarks are mostly government targets with an independent source, so the risk is lower, but they have not been checked against the CBGDP.

v19: The remaining 15 CBDP-benchmarked CCC rows re-derived against the CBGDP (October 2025) and the CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report; the v17 SUPERSEDED marker is now cleared from all 24. ELEVEN are fully re-derived: IND-C-006 offshore wind (Clean Power 2030: 43-50 GW by 2030, replacing "50 GW including 5 GW floating"), IND-C-008 solar (45-47 GW by 2030 is a GOVERNMENT ambition - this row previously mislabelled it a CCC pathway figure - and the 70 GW by 2035 Net Zero Strategy figure is not the current benchmark), IND-C-012 CfD (AR7 record 8.2 GW fixed plus 0.2 GW floating, replacing the AR4 reference), IND-C-028 industry (no CBGDP energy-intensity target; electrification is the primary route, Balanced Pathway 36% of industrial energy demand electric by 2030 against 27% in 2024), IND-C-034 agriculture, IND-C-035 peatland (combined four-administration ambition; 21,400 ha in 2025), IND-C-036 tree planting (combined UK ambition; 15,600 ha in 2024/25, down 25%), IND-C-039 SFI (reopening June 2026), IND-C-041 SAF (full mandate structure including the HEFA cap and the power-to-liquid obligation), IND-C-045 and IND-C-047 waste. FOUR ARE PARTIAL and say so in Source_Reference: IND-C-030 CCS and IND-C-031 hydrogen, where the CCC states the CBGDP attributes less abatement to both than the CBDP did but the CBGDP’s own figures were not read; IND-C-038 fertiliser, where no successor target was found and the CCC carries no such indicator; and IND-C-055 energy productivity, where the National Energy Efficiency Target could not be confirmed as current. Those four record the direction of change rather than a re-derived number, deliberately, rather than carrying a figure nobody has checked. ALSO CORRECTED: IND-C-014 read "ban on new petrol/diesel cars by 2035"; the phase-out of new petrol and diesel CARS is 2030, with 2035 applying to vans. Found while doing this work and outside the original scope.

v20: The four PARTIAL benchmarks resolved by reading the CBGDP itself - the Section 14 Report and its technical annex - rather than the CCC’s commentary on it. THE MAIN FINDING IS NEGATIVE AND WORTH STATING PLAINLY: for three of the four, the CBGDP sets no target at all, so the figures these rows carried were not merely out of date but had no current government referent. IND-C-031 hydrogen - the CBGDP sets NO capacity target; production capacity is DERIVED FROM MODELLED DEMAND assuming supply equals demand, with blue plants at a 90% load factor and green at 60%, and delivery runs through allocation rounds (HAR1 11 projects, HAR2 27 shortlisted, HAR3 by 2026, HAR4 from 2028). A new Hydrogen Strategy is in preparation. The 10 GW by 2030 came from the 2021 Hydrogen Strategy and is not restated. IND-C-038 fertiliser - no quantified target; nitrous oxide is addressed through named advice-and-guidance policies with market-led uptake (agronomist-led nutrient management plans, precision farming with variable-rate nitrogen technology, grass and herbal leys, clover at 20%+ of mixed grassland, slurry nitrogen analysis). IND-C-055 energy productivity - the 15% final-energy-demand reduction target appears in NEITHER the Section 14 Report NOR the technical annex; the CBGDP works through sectoral policy lines instead. IND-C-030 CCS is the one row with a real number: the Track-1 clusters enable up to 4 MtCO2/year (East Coast) and 4.5 MtCO2/year (HyNet) at full utilisation, about 8.5 MtCO2/year combined, against £9.4 billion allocated at Spending Review 2025, with Track-2 (Acorn, Viking) FID due later this Parliament and gas-terminal CCUS from 2034 - an order of magnitude below the 20-30 MtCO2/year by 2030 this row previously carried from the Net Zero Strategy 2021. NO ROW ON THIS SHEET NOW CARRIES A SUPERSEDED OR UNVERIFIED BENCHMARK.

v21: ALL 173 SDG Indicators rows climate-scored. They were the only records in the workbook with Climate_Score blank, and because build_indicator_finder.py read the score through cell_int(), which returns 0 for a blank, those 173 records - 18% of the catalogue - rendered in the dashboard as climate score 0, indistinguishable from the 283 records assessed and genuinely scored zero. A user filtering for climate-relevant indicators was silently excluding a sixth of the workbook that had never been assessed. Climate_Score, Climate_Dependency and Climate_Rationale are now populated on every row. Distribution: 113 score 0, 36 score 1, 20 score 2, 4 score 3 - which is what the SDG framework should look like, since most of it is social, economic and statistical rather than environmental. METHOD: the Legend scale was applied as a MEASURED-QUANTITY test (does climate or weather data enter the calculation, or does inter-annual weather move the value), not a topical-relevance test. 29 of the 173 are identical indicators to records already scored elsewhere in this workbook - the GBF monitoring framework reuses SDG indicators - and those were ANCHORED on the existing score rather than rescored, with the sibling record cited in the rationale and marked "A:". The 3s are 6.4.2 water stress, 6.6.1 water-related ecosystem extent, 11.6.2 PM2.5/PM10 and 14.3.1 marine acidity. TWO CROSS-SHEET INCONSISTENCIES FOUND AND LOGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the same emissions indicator is scored 1 on the CCC, JNCC and EEA sheets but 3 at [GBF-184], and PM2.5 is scored 3 at [IND-E-003], 2 at [GBF-074] and 1 on the IPBES sheet. Within-sheet coherence was chosen over importing the divergence: SDG emissions rows follow the 1, and PM2.5 follows the 3. A harmonisation pass across all nine sheets is queued. STILL BLANK on this sheet, unchanged: NCF_Category and Indicator_Type (173 rows each), and GBF_Targets_Clean is absent from the sheet entirely.

v22: NCF_Category and Indicator_Type populated on all 173 SDG Indicators rows, the last two blank columns on that sheet. NCF_Category is a CONTROLLED five-term vocabulary and is now validated by the check_links controlled-vocabulary invariant on these rows for the first time. Distribution: Enabling 128, Benefit 18, Pressure 18, State - Habitats 6, State - Species 3. The heavy weighting to Enabling is correct rather than lazy: the NCF Legend defines Enabling as policy responses, governance metrics, funding, data and public engagement, and most of the SDG framework is social, economic, financial or statistical. It matches how the workbook already treats the CBD GBF sheet (102 of 202 Enabling) and BIP (34 of 81). ANCHORING: for the 29 rows that duplicate a GBF or BIP record, NCF_Category was taken from the sibling rather than reassigned, and every one of those anchors agreed with the value derived independently. Indicator_Type was NOT anchored, because the CBD GBF sheet stores the GBF monitoring-framework TIER there (Headline / Component / Complementary / Binary), which is a framework tier and not a type; carrying those onto SDG rows would have been meaningless. Instead the cross-sheet generic typology was used - Policy / governance metric, Pressure / threat index, Ecosystem service flow, Habitat extent / condition, Species index / trend, Expenditure, Consumption footprint, Emissions, Water quality, Deployment / uptake, Demand / activity, Intensity metric, Human wellbeing / engagement - with TWO NEW TERMS COINED because nothing existing fitted: "Socio-economic statistic" (52 rows: poverty, employment, income, trade, macroeconomic and statistical measures, which are not policy metrics and not natural-capital measures) and "Hazard impact" (5 rows: the Sendai disaster mortality and economic loss indicators, which appear three times each across goals 1, 11 and 13). Indicator_Type is declared FREE TEXT in the Data Dictionary so neither coinage needed vocabulary approval, but both are flagged in Data/pending_additions.md for confirmation, since coining terms across 57 records is the kind of thing that should be visible rather than absorbed. The IFW-08 register warning flags for these two columns have been replaced with the computed summaries. STILL OPEN on this sheet: GBF_Targets_Clean is absent entirely, which is a column addition rather than a fill.

v23: IFW-10 re-extracted against the CCC Adaptation Monitoring Framework of 20 May 2026. THE CENTRAL FINDING IS STRUCTURAL: the current framework publishes NO INDICATOR LIST. Its fourteen system monitoring maps publish an objective, proposed targets, actions, enablers and policies; the CCC selects indicators against those targets separately in each adaptation progress report. So the 32 rows previously held could not be refreshed indicator-for-indicator, because there is nothing to refresh them against. What the framework does publish, and what is now held, are the PROPOSED TARGETS - measurable and time-bound, and the closest analogue to the target rows already on this sheet. 38 new records, IND-C-147 to IND-C-184, one per proposed target, across all fourteen systems: health 3, built environment and communities 2, public services 3, cultural heritage 2, water and wastewater 3, energy 2, transport 3, waste 2, digital and telecoms 1, land 4, sea 2, food security 2, economy and finance 7, national security and international engagement 2. SCOPE: all fourteen systems were taken, not a climate-nature subset, applying the tiered triage decision already made for the policy scan - catalogue broadly, score climate relevance at entry, let the dashboards filter. Nine of the fourteen systems had no representation at all before this. Climate scores: 24 at 3, 10 at 2, 4 at 1 - high, as expected, because most adaptation targets are defined in directly climatic terms (excess heat-related mortality, resilience to a 1 in 500-year drought, flood probability thresholds). Data_Source is recorded as to be confirmed on every row, deliberately: the framework names no data series, and inventing one would be a guess. THE 32 LEGACY ROWS ARE RETAINED and now have their own register record, IFW-11 "CCC Adaptation Monitoring Framework 2023-2025 (superseded)", so the register shows both vintages honestly instead of one record spanning two frameworks. Sheet total rises from 947 to 985 indicator records; the register TOTAL row now reads 11 frameworks across 9 sheets.

v24: IND-E-042 linked to the new [POL-070] NaFRA2 record in UK governance v26 - Policy_Links gains the code and Data_Source now names where the assessment is held. The indicator remains the measure; the assessment behind it is now a governance record rather than a bare mention in a text field.

v25: Source_Framework values aligned between the CCC rows and the register, so the indicator finder can join them. The finder now derives each framework’s policy-context chain from the register rather than from a hardcoded table, and that join is on Source_Framework - which exposed two mismatches left behind by the v17 split. (1) The 79 mitigation rows still read "CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework / UK Net Zero Strategy" while [IFW-02] had been renamed "CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework"; the rows are now aligned. (2) [IFW-11] read "CCC Adaptation Monitoring Framework 2023-2025 (superseded)" while its 32 rows read the same name without the suffix; the suffix is removed from the register, where Policy_Purpose already states the framework is superseded, rather than editing 32 rows to carry a status word in a name field. Before this alignment both groups of rows - 111 of the 149 on the sheet - would have rendered with an EMPTY policy context panel. No indicator values changed.

v26: Two more Source_Framework mismatches aligned, found by the warning added to build_indicator_finder.py in v25. The CBD GBF rows read "CBD Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF)" and the SDG rows read "UN SDG Global Indicator Framework", while [IFW-05] and [IFW-08] carry "CBD Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF)" and "UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)". Because the finder now joins rows to their register row on this column, all 375 of those rows would have rendered with an EMPTY policy context panel. Row values are aligned to the register, which is the canonical name list; where the framework’s own fuller title carries useful precision - the SDG set is strictly the global INDICATOR framework rather than the goals - that belongs in the register’s Policy_Purpose, which already says so, not in a join key. Counting v25, 486 of the 985 rows had a Source_Framework that did not match any register row; none of this was visible before the join existed. No indicator values changed.

v27: Climate_Score HARMONISED across all nine framework sheets. The v21 SDG pass found the same measured quantity scored differently on different sheets (GHG emissions 1 and 3; PM2.5 1, 2 and 3; protected-area coverage 0 and 3), and a full review of all 985 records showed THREE READINGS OF THE SCALE IN USE: (a) the Legend as written - do climate/weather data enter the calculation, or does inter-annual weather move the value; (b) 'climate change is a threat driver', which scored Red List, RLE and habitat-extent measures 2 on the BIP, IPBES and GBF sheets although the Legend's own example puts conservation status at 1; (c) 'relevant to climate policy', which scored the 2023-25 CCC adaptation rows (IFW-11) 3 for protected-area extent, water-infrastructure capacity and carbon-code registries, and scored GHG emissions 3 at GBF-184 and IPBES-D-023. Reading (a) is adopted; topical climate relevance is carried by Policy_Sector = Climate, not by this score. 162 records changed (145 down, 16 up; 98 high and 64 medium confidence), with Climate_Dependency and Climate_Rationale rewritten on each: CCC 54, CBD GBF 31, SDG 19, IPBES 17, EIF 14, BIP 12, JNCC 8, SoN 4, EEA 3. Workbook distribution 0/1/2/3 moves from 396/233/228/128 to 435/269/201/80. Resolved: all GHG-emission inventory records 1 (temperature-adjusted series 3); all air-pollutant concentrations 2; all protected-area coverage 0; every Red List Index disaggregation 1 except reef-building corals 2; climate-policy administrative counts (NDCs, DRR strategies, adaptation plans, climate finance, carbon-code registries, 'assets assessed and adapted') 0; renewable-generation shares 2. NEW ON THE LEGEND SHEET: a Core principle and Rules A-H below the 0-3 scale, so the reading is written down rather than inferred from examples. Rule labels deliberately do not begin with a digit, because build_indicator_finder.py lifts the scale from Legend rows matching ^[0-3]. Data Dictionary Climate_Score row updated in place. Ten borderline records deliberately NOT changed are listed with reasons on the 'Kept - flagged' sheet of outputs_other/climate_score_harmonisation/climate_score_harmonisation_proposal.xlsx, which is the full review record (old and new score and rationale for every changed row). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FINDER: a 'climate score >= N' filter no longer returns climate-policy administrative measures; filter on Policy_Sector = Climate for topical relevance. IND-C-176 and IND-C-177 do not carry Climate in Policy_Sector.
